3 1. For the sake of convenience, brevity and handiness the instant petitions are disposed of by way of this common judgment. It is made clear that the same shall be applicable on all of the petitions on mutatis mutandis basis. 
2. In S.B. Civil Writ Petition No. 16686/2018, vide order dated 02.08.2018, the Court had granted interim protection by staying the operation of transfer order dated 12 th July, 2018. Ever since then no sincere efforts are made to contest the instant matter. 
3. Nevertheless, on the directions of the Court the instant matters pertaining to transfer issues are on the board after a lapse of six years. 
4. Learned counsel representing the State has averred that in majority of matters under the garb of the interim protection, the petitioners are rendering service at the erstwhile place of posting, which causes an impediment in the smooth functioning of the departments. 
5. Considering the fact that after attaining the interim protections the matters are on board after a lapse of six years and the submissions [2024:RJ-JP:49582] (5 of 5) [CW-16686/2018] averred by the learned counsel for the respondents, this Court is of the view that with efflux of time, much water would have flown however, without commenting upon the merits/demerits of the instant matter(s) and placing reliance upon the ratio encapsulated in Shilpi Bose & Ors. Vs. State of Bihar &
ors. reported in 1991 Supp (2) SCC 659, the respondents are granted a liberty to pass appropriate orders considering the administrative exigencies; strictly, in accordance with law. The relevant extract from the afore-cited ratio is reproduced herein below: 
"4. In our opinion, the courts should not interfere with a transfer order which is made in public interest and for administrative reasons unless the transfer orders are made in violation of any mandatory statutory rule or on the ground of mala fide. A government servant holding a transferable post has no vested right to remain posted at one place or the other, he is liable to be transferred from one place to the other. 
Transfer orders issued by the competent authority do not violate any of his legal rights. Even if a transfer order is passed in violation of executive instructions or orders, the courts ordinarily should not interfere with the order instead affected party should approach the higher authorities in the department. If the courts continue to interfere with day-to-day transfer orders issued by the government and its subordinate authorities, there will be complete chaos in the administration which would not be conducive to public interest. The High Court overlooked these aspects in interfering with the transfer orders." 
6. Accordingly, the present petitions are disposed of with the aforementioned directions. Pending applications, if any, shall stand disposed of. 
(SAMEER JAIN),J DEEPAK/10-12, 14-17 Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
